children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--Canola futures on the Intercontinental Exchange declined on Friday while comparable oils were mostly negative.
Crude oil was lower, which weighed on the Chicago soy complex and Malaysian palm oil, but European rapeseed was higher.
An analyst said warm temperatures and sunny skies throughout the Prairies over the next few days will help advance the region's canola harvest and pressure prices.
The Canadian Grain Commission reported a negligible amount of canola exports during the week ended Sept. 13, but year-to-date totals were up slightly at 709,600 ton.
At mid-afternoon, the Canadian dollar was down less than one-tenth of a U.S. cent compared to Thursday's close.
There were 44,990 canola contracts traded on Friday, compared to Thursday when 49,230 contracts changed hands. Spreads accounted for 25,140 contracts in today's trade.
